overall: The AG found no improper pre-meeting deliberation but found a violation for omitting a reasonably anticipated topic from the May 10, 2012 notice; the committee's prompt remediation was credited, and it was ordered to comply in future.

allegations.summary: Alleged the committee deliberated outside a posted meeting before May 10, 2012, when it voted to eliminate the Director of Safety and Security position.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find evidence to support the assertion that the Committee improperly deliberated in advance of the May 10, 2012 meeting.

allegations.summary: Alleged the elimination of the Director position was left off the May 10, 2012 special budget meeting notice, though the chair anticipated discussing it.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law, however, by failing to include a topic in its meeting notice that the Chair reasonably anticipated at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that the Ethics Commission be directed to conduct a formal investigation of the committee's conduct.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government only enforces and interprets the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, and does not have jurisdiction to order the Ethics Commission to conduct an investigation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, ordered in addition to the committee's own remedial steps (reconsideration of the vote, a subcommittee, and an OML presentation).
remedy_passage: In addition to the remedial steps already taken by the Committee, we order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Committee that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
